The comparison display includes Earthworm, Snail, Slug, and Centipede. Earthworm is an annelid, Snail and Slug are mollusks, and Centipede is a many-legged arthropod. These comparison animals are not insects despite the unit’s broad exhibit theme. Millipede is a many-segmented arthropod with two leg pairs on most apparent segments, not an insect. Aphid, Praying Mantis, and Firefly are insects; Firefly belongs to the beetle family commonly associated with bioluminescence. The guide contrasts Moth, a member of the butterfly-and-moth order, with Wasp, a member of a different insect group. Night activity alone is not a universal moth identifier, and the guide uses reliable species references rather than a simple color rule.
